literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) describe C-terminal tags on POPDC1 or its chicken ortholog Bves. Per the authoritative topology, the C-terminus (residues 114–360) is entirely intracellular — the large Popeye cAMP-binding domain faces the cytoplasm. A C-terminal Flag (L1/L2/L3) or ECFP (L4) therefore sits on the intracellular face and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. The membrane-localized 'wire-mesh' immunostaining in L1 reflects the protein's junctional trafficking, not extracellular display of the Flag epitope. The only extracellular spans are residues 1–39 (N-terminal) and 87–92 (a 6-residue loop between TM2 and TM3); neither is supported by any ledger insertion. No ledger line grounds an N-terminal prepend or an insertion in the extracellular loop. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal Flag tag on full-length chicken Bves (POPDC1 ortholog) localizes to cell membrane but the C-terminus (residues 114–360) is intracellular per topology; the tag is on the cytoplasmic face, not the extracellular surface.

C-terminal ECFP fusion to full-length human POPDC1 (pECFP-N1 vector); the C-terminus is intracellular (residues 114–360), so the fluorescent protein tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
